claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/
The post at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration from CDK to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS and multi-cloud with CDK was nearly impossible.
AWS CDK allows developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
Pulumi supports any programming language, while AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because of direct execution rather than CloudFormation.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets management.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
SST Ion is the code name for a new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS is described in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its deployment state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications, with components defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi, as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation.
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine, which calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' says SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and the deployment engine, and Terraform providers are bridged through Pulumi.
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says the imports from Pulumi mean the whole deployment process is built on Pulumi.
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds and more, and the Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
The SST repository is now at anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API works by embedding Pulumi programs inside other tools.
The Pulumi engine handles diffing desired versus actual state, dependency graph building, operation ordering, preview and diff, and state tracking.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state that 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Nitric and Defang run application deployments through the Pulumi engine and its provider bridge.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) downloads in the week of September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode now has a larger GitHub following than SST itself.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
SST's dependency on the Pulumi engine and its release cadence haven't changed since the team's attention broadened to opencode.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
